models.title: TEACHER ONLY · IELTS listening Part 1 script (gym membership)

block.label: TEACHER ONLY · LISTENING PART 1 SCRIPT
block.html: Do not share the screen. Read once, at normal speed.

items.a:
Receptionist: Good morning, Riverside Sports Centre. How can I help you?
Caller: Hi. I'd like to join the gym, please.
Receptionist: Of course. Can I have your full name?
Caller: It's Daniel Whitmore.
Receptionist: Could you spell your surname?
Caller: W-H-I-T-M-O-R-E.
Receptionist: Thank you. And your date of birth?
Caller: The fourteenth of March, nineteen ninety-six.
Receptionist: And a contact number?
Caller: Yes, it's oh-seven-nine, double four, three-one-two, eight-six-five.
Receptionist: Which membership would you like? Basic is twenty-five pounds a month, and Premium is thirty-nine.
Caller: What's the difference?
Receptionist: Premium includes the swimming pool and all the classes.
Caller: I really want to swim, so... Premium, please.
Receptionist: Great. When would you like to start? Next week?
Caller: Next week... oh no, sorry, I'm away then. The week after, on the twenty-first.
Receptionist: Perfect, the twenty-first. And how did you hear about us? Online?
Caller: No, a colleague recommended you.
Receptionist: Lovely. On your first visit, please bring a photo ID, like your passport, and a towel.
Caller: Great, thanks. See you on the twenty-first!

models.title: TEACHER ONLY · IELTS listening Part 2 script (museum)

block.label: TEACHER ONLY · LISTENING PART 2 SCRIPT
block.html: Do not share the screen. Read once.

items.a:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Harbour Museum. Before you start, a few words about the building and the visit. Many people think this building was a shipyard, because of the old boats outside, but in fact it was the city's fish market until the museum opened here in 1987.

Most visitors start on the ground floor, but I'd suggest going straight up to the top floor first. The views are nice, but that's not the reason: the ships gallery up there gets very crowded after eleven o'clock, when the school groups arrive.

The café is next to the gift shop on the ground floor. Please note that it closes at half past four, half an hour before the museum itself closes.

Finally, you can take photos anywhere you like, even in the ships gallery, except in the map room. The old maps are very sensitive to light, so no photos there, please. Enjoy your visit!

models.title: IELTS reading · why cities are planting trees (passage)

block.label: READING · ABOUT 15 MINUTES
block.html:
Why cities are planting trees

A On a summer afternoon, the centre of a large city is often several degrees warmer than the countryside around it, and the difference is usually even greater at night. This effect, known as the urban heat island, happens because concrete, brick and asphalt absorb heat from the sun during the day and release it slowly after dark.

B Trees reduce this heat in two ways. First, their shade stops sunlight before it reaches roads and walls, so these surfaces stay much cooler than surfaces in direct sun. Second, trees release water through their leaves, and as this water evaporates, it cools the air around them.

C The benefits are not only about temperature. Tree roots and soil absorb rainwater, which lowers the risk of flooding after heavy storms, and leaves can trap some of the dust in polluted air. Researchers have also linked green streets with lower stress levels and with more people choosing to walk.

D However, planting trees in a city is not simple. Roots need space underground, where they compete with pipes and cables. Young trees need regular watering for their first few years, and many die when this care stops. Choosing the wrong species can also create problems, such as roots that break pavements or trees that need too much water in a dry climate.

E For this reason, many planners now argue that planting is only the first step. In their view, what matters most is choosing the right tree for the right place, and then looking after it until it can survive on its own.

models.title: IELTS writing Task 1 · say it before you write it

block.label: TASK 1 · SAY IT FIRST
block.html: Say each part. Then reveal a model.

items.a: The table compares the average summer temperatures in three parts of a city in the afternoon and late at night.
Overall, the city centre was the hottest area at both times, while the park was the coolest, and all three areas were considerably cooler at night.
At 3 p.m., the city centre reached 36°C, three degrees more than the residential area and six degrees more than the park.
At night, the temperature fell in all three areas, but the drop was smallest in the city centre (7 degrees), where it remained at 29°C.

models.title: IELTS writing Task 2 · trees or public transport (discuss both views)

block.label: WRITING TASK 2 · ABOUT 40 MINUTES · 250+ WORDS
block.html:
Some people think that city governments should spend money on planting trees, while others believe this money should be spent on public transport.

Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

models.title: IELTS writing Task 2 · a clear structure

block.label: TASK 2 · FOUR PARAGRAPHS
block.html: Plan it aloud. Then reveal a model sentence.

items.a: Cities have limited budgets, and there is some debate about whether trees or public transport should come first. In my view, both matter, but transport should be the priority.
On the one hand, trees make streets cooler and more pleasant, which encourages people to walk instead of driving.
On the other hand, good buses and trains reduce traffic and pollution for millions of people every day.
In conclusion, although trees bring real benefits, I believe public transport should receive the larger share of the money.

lesson.title: IELTS Trial Class: All Four Skills
lesson.subtitle: Speaking · listening · reading · writing · how it is marked
lesson.plan: Aula experimental de diagnóstico, uma amostra curta de cada parte (uns 60 min). NÃO compartilhe a tela nos blocos TEACHER ONLY: os 2 roteiros da escuta (leia cada um uma vez, em ritmo normal), a tabela de conversão de nota e o que observar. Ordem: objetivo do aluno → formato da prova → Speaking 1 → Listening (12 questões) → Reading (12 questões, 15 min) → Writing (Task 1 em voz alta, Task 2 planejada, ele escreve introdução e overview) → Speaking 2 e 3 → critérios e devolutiva.
